Hirschheim: a town of timber halls under trees older than
any kingdom, lanterns in the branches, and beastkin with
wolf ears and deer ears watching you from every door.

I promised. When we had the second one.
Seven hundred and thirty-five years ago I was a general
of the Dawn Host. Sōryū Akira's general. One of five.
The Demon Lord had burned my city when I was nine. I
wanted every demon in the world dead, and everything that
had touched one, and everything that might, later.
So I purged. Villages the miasma had brushed. Wells. Once
a whole valley, because two of the dead there had been
seen to twitch. The Death arts, you've seen them. I was
Akira took my command away at Frostheim, the last winter
of the war. In front of the Host. I was dying by then,
a spear through me, and I was so angry I couldn't see.
Something came to me, lying there in the snow. A merchant
in brass, with a contract for anger. Keep fighting, he
said. Forever. Purge everything. Only sign.
Akira tore the contract out of my hands. She refused it
for me. So I died, angry, unbought, and I stayed angry
for seven hundred years, in the dark, until a thread
pulled tight and there was a girl with a light in her
hand, waking up in a cave.
"The General who was refused." That's what he calls me.
He's right. It's the best thing anyone ever did for me.
…Less, my Lord. Less every day. Don't tell anyone.
